discussion_comments.comment_body: Confirmed this is not used at runtime — the integration pushes via the DCR / Logs Ingestion API using an AAD bearer token, so workspace shared keys are never read. I am deferring the removal in this PR: the data-connector validator's RestAPI permission template *requires* the connector to declare `sharedKeys`, and the action also lives in our authoritative `roles.sh` / Terraform / CLI sources. I would rather remove it as a deliberate cross-artifact change than introduce a connector-vs-role mismatch here. Open to guidance on the right permission pattern for a DCR-push / RBAC connector that fits neither the RestAPI nor AzureFunction template.

I added SystemAssigned Identity but, during deployment, i got:
Resource type 'Microsoft.Resources/deploymentScripts' does not support creation of 'SystemAssigned' resource identity. The supported types are 'UserAssigned'. (Code: CannotSetResourceIdentity)
I removed the identity. It was working without it and this is a simple sleep for 30 seconds script. If the identity section is a hard requirement, please advise the best option that do not force customers to provide additional information.

Fixed! Updated the `Description` to match the actual resources (OIDC web identity provider only).

The role is intentionally not in this template: this is Template 1 of the two-template AWS S3 connector setup, where Template 1 creates the account-level OIDC provider and Template 2 creates the IAM assumed role + S3/SQS resources. The provider is a per-account singleton (one per issuer URL) and is meant to be skipped if one already exists, so adding the role here would be incorrect.
